description: Monitor the machine VS Code is connected to (Remote-SSH, WSL, Tunnel, Dev Containers or local): CPU, GPUs, memory, disks, network, processes, tmux, ports, Docker and more, with very low overhead.
viewContainer.title: Server Monitor
welcome.tmux:
No tmux sessions on this machine.
[New Session](command:serverMonitor.tmux.new)
Sessions keep running after you disconnect: start long jobs in one, then attach, peek at the output, or get notified when they finish.
welcome.du:
Find out what is using disk space, one folder level at a time (like ncdu). Scans run du in the background and never cross into other filesystems.
[Analyze Folder…](command:serverMonitor.du.analyze)
[Analyze Home Folder](command:serverMonitor.du.analyzeHome)
You can also right-click a folder in the Explorer, or a mount point in the Disks view.
welcome.watches:
No active watches.
To get notified when a long job ends, right-click a process in the Processes, GPUs or Users view and choose "Notify When Process Exits", or right-click a tmux pane that is running a command and choose "Notify When Command Finishes". Watches keep running while the window is in the background.
[Notify When GPUs Are Free…](command:serverMonitor.watchFreeGpus)
Memory and disk usage alerts are on by default; change the thresholds in [Settings](command:serverMonitor.openSettings).

config.title: Server Monitor
config.refreshInterval: Refresh interval in milliseconds for CPU, memory, network and GPU metrics while the window is focused. Process, port, tmux and disk lists use their own, slower intervals.
config.backgroundMode: What to do while the VS Code window is not focused. Watches and threshold alerts always keep running at `#serverMonitor.backgroundInterval#`.
config.backgroundMode.slow: Keep refreshing, but only at the background interval.
config.backgroundMode.pause: Pause the views and the status bar until the window is focused again.
config.backgroundInterval: Refresh interval in milliseconds while the window is not focused (see `#serverMonitor.backgroundMode#`). Watches and threshold alerts also use this interval.
config.statusBar.enabled: Show a compact resource summary in the status bar. Hover it for details, click it to open the dashboard.
config.statusBar.items: Metrics shown in the status bar entry, in this order.
config.statusBar.items.gpuMem: GPU memory usage across all GPUs
config.statusBar.items.disk: Usage of the disk that holds your home folder
config.statusBar.warnPercent: Memory or home-disk usage (%) at which the status bar entry turns yellow. CPU is not taken into account: a busy compute server is normal.
config.statusBar.critPercent: Memory or home-disk usage (%) at which the status bar entry turns red.
config.gpu.freeMemoryMiB: A GPU counts as free when less than this much memory (MiB) is in use and its utilization is below `#serverMonitor.gpu.freeUtilPercent#`.
config.gpu.freeUtilPercent: A GPU counts as free when its utilization (%) is below this value and its memory use is below `#serverMonitor.gpu.freeMemoryMiB#`.
config.alerts.enabled: Warn when memory or a disk is nearly full (thresholds below). Each alert fires once per crossing and can be muted per machine and disk.
config.alerts.memoryPercent: Warn when memory usage reaches this percentage.
config.alerts.diskPercent: Warn when any monitored disk reaches this percentage.
config.processes.defaultScope: Which processes the Processes view shows when it opens.
config.processes.limit: Maximum number of processes listed before the rest is collapsed into a "more…" entry. Larger values cost more per refresh.
config.disk.excludeFsTypes: Additional filesystem types to hide from the Disks view, e.g. `nfs4` or `fuse.sshfs`. Pseudo filesystems (proc, sysfs, tmpfs, squashfs, overlay, …) are always hidden, except `/dev/shm`.
config.disk.excludeMounts: Mount points (and everything below them) to hide from the Disks view, e.g. `/mnt/archive`.
config.disk.networkTimeoutMs: Timeout in milliseconds for querying network filesystems (NFS, CIFS, sshfs, …). A mount that does not answer in time is shown as not responding and retried with backoff, so a hung NFS server never blocks the extension.
config.docker.enabled: Show Docker containers when a Docker socket is found. The extension talks to the Docker Engine API over the socket; the `docker` CLI is only needed for Follow Logs and Open Shell.
config.history.minutes: How many minutes of CPU, memory, network and GPU history the dashboard charts keep.
config.quickCommands: Quick commands shown on the sidebar panel's Tools → Common page. Each runs in a new integrated terminal on the connected machine. Example: `{ "name": "GPU", "command": "watch -n 1 nvidia-smi" }`.
config.sidebar.showTreeViews: Also show the classic tree views (GPUs, Processes, tmux, Ports, Disks, Users, Docker, Folder Sizes, Watches) with their right-click menus below the sidebar panel. The panel itself has a page for each of them.
